parts.title: Saving The Skink
parts.article:
(A) New Zealand’s reptiles come in three forms: the tuatara, the geckos and the skinks. With their gleaming scales, long bodies and often surprisingly short limbs, skinks are instantly recognisable. There are more than 90 species, half of which still await formal description. Identification depends on where specimens are found, and such minutiae as the number of scales on their toes. Two of the largest species of skink--the grand and the Otago--are found only in Otago, in New Zealand’s South Island.

(B) Skinks, being reptiles, need to regulate their temperature, and lie on sunny rocks to absorb heat. However, the grand and Otago are the only kinds that do not hibernate through winter; when snow can fall even in summer in Otago, there is no point in them lying dormant for extended periods. Like all other New Zealand reptiles except tuatara and the egg-laying Suter’s skink, they give birth to tiny baby lizards. Today, the Otago and grand skinks are lucky to reach five years of age in the wild, although in zoos or research centres they can live beyond thirty.

(C) Unfortunately, extinction may loom for these reptiles. With any decline in New Zealand fauna, predation is always suspected, so the efforts of the Department of Conservation (DOC) have focused on controlling specific pests. An example was a six-year project to control the feral cats on the Otago Skink Reserve, launched in the 1990s. Despite the capture of hundreds of cats, skinks showed no signs of recovery. Indeed, there were further declines. The trapping programme also revealed rats and hedgehogs to be predators.

(D) Parasite infections are also thought to be on the rise. Although no direct health implications have been detected the trend is a concern, as it may signal a subtle deterioration in the skinks’ living environment. Infection with mites is suspected of inhibiting reproduction among captive animals.

(E) Another potential threat is habitat loss. Eight hundred years ago, Otago was covered in forest. However, extensive burning produced wide open tussock country. The skinks’ response to this change isn’t known, nor what their habitat was in the earlier environment, with its predominance of shrubs and trees. Furthermore, recent intensive farming has led to poor soil. Even if we had the answer to the eradication of predators, we haven’t a clue to the habitat we should be recreating for the skinks, or if where they persist is best for conservation.

(F) It is also puzzling that grand and Otago skinks have persisted only in small, isolated populations on rocky outcrops. Why they cannot survive in the surrounding grassland, which appears similar in many respects, is unknown. Climate change poses a further, longer-term threat, potentially altering temperature patterns and food availability in ways that may not favor these specialist reptiles. A lack of fundamental knowledge about their ecology--what they eat, how they interact with other species, and their precise microhabitat needs--makes effective conservation planning difficult. Current efforts involve a combination of captive breeding programs, predator-free fencing around key sites, and ongoing research. The survival of these unique skinks will depend on solving the complex puzzle of intertwined threats, from predators and parasites to habitat degradation and our own limited understanding.

Questions 32-35
Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage?
In boxes 32–35 on your answer sheet, write:

Q32 Over half of New Zealand’s skink species have been formally named and described.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q33 The program to control feral cats in the 1990s was successful in helping the skink population recover.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q34 Mite infections have been proven to cause health problems for wild skinks.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q35 Scientists know what the ideal habitat for the skinks’ conservation should be.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN
Questions 36-40
Choose the correct letter A, B, C or D.

Q36 What is the main reason given for the skinks’ poor survival rate in the wild?

  • A Lack of food
  • B Predation
  • C Extreme winter temperatures
  • D Competition with other lizards

Q37 According to the passage, what does the rise in parasite infections possibly indicate?

  • A An increase in the skink population
  • B An improvement in the skinks’ environment
  • C A decline in the quality of the skinks’ habitat
  • D The success of captive breeding programs

Q38 The transformation of Otago’s landscape 800 years ago involved:

  • A The planting of forests
  • B The creation of farmland
  • C Extensive burning
  • D The introduction of predators

Q39 What does the writer identify as a major obstacle to conserving the skinks?

  • A A lack of funding
  • B Public apathy
  • C Insufficient scientific knowledge
  • D Conflict with farmers

Q40 Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a current conservation effort?

  • A Building predator-free fences
  • B Captive breeding programs
  • C Relocating skinks to new islands
  • D Ongoing research

reference:
Q27

解析 原文提到这两种石龙子是新西兰最大的“物种”（species）之二。

干扰 你可能想填“skinks”，但原文说是“最大的石龙子物种（species of skink）”，顺着题目的“largest”往后找，直接填“物种（species）”最符合句意。

句子 Two of the largest species of skink--the grand and the Otago--are found only in Otago, in New Zealand’s South Island.

Q28

解析 原文明确指出，与其他大多数种类不同，它们在冬天不会“冬眠”（hibernate）。

干扰 你可能想找“lie dormant”，但题目要求填写的字数受限，且“hibernate”直接对应题目的“冬眠”这个核心动作。

句子 Skinks, being reptiles, need to regulate their temperature, and lie on sunny rocks to absorb heat. However, the grand and Otago are the only kinds that do not hibernate through winter; when snow can fall even in summer in Otago, there is no point in them lying dormant for extended periods.

Q29

解析 原文提到它们直接生小蜥蜴，这与产卵的“Suter's skink”完全不同。

干扰 你可能会漏掉撇号或者大写，记得在填空题中完全照抄原文的专有名词和标点，千万别自己乱改。

句子 Like all other New Zealand reptiles except tuatara and the egg-laying Suter’s skink, they give birth to tiny baby lizards.

Q30

解析 原文说它们在野外活到“五”（five）岁就算幸运了，说明其寿命很少超过五年。

干扰 你可能会看到后面的“thirty”，但那是它们在动物园里的寿命，一定要看清题目问的是野外（in the wild）。

句子 Today, the Otago and grand skinks are lucky to reach five years of age in the wild, although in zoos or research centres they can live beyond thirty.

Q31

解析 原文指出，诱捕项目发现老鼠和“刺猬”（hedgehogs）也是捕食者。

干扰 你可能会填cats，但题目已经用“aside from cats”排除了猫，顺着往下找别的捕食动物就能找到刺猬。

句子 An example was a six-year project to control the feral cats on the Otago Skink Reserve, launched in the 1990s. Despite the capture of hundreds of cats, skinks showed no signs of recovery. Indeed, there were further declines. The trapping programme also revealed rats and hedgehogs to be predators.

Q32

解析 原文指出有半数的物种“还在等待”正式描述，这意味着被正式描述的并没有“超过半数”（over half）。

干扰 你可能会看到“half”就匆忙选了YES，但没注意到原文的“await”（等待）一词直接推翻了题目“已经被描述”的说法。

句子 There are more than 90 species, half of which still await formal description. Identification depends on where specimens are found, and such minutiae as the number of scales on their toes.

Q33

解析 原文明确说到，尽管抓了成百上千只野猫，石龙子的数量依然没有恢复的迹象。

干扰 你可能看到提到了“控制野猫项目”就想当然觉得成功了，做题时一定要往后多读一句看看最终结果。

句子 An example was a six-year project to control the feral cats on the Otago Skink Reserve, launched in the 1990s. Despite the capture of hundreds of cats, skinks showed no signs of recovery. Indeed, there were further declines.

Q34

解析 原文说螨虫感染只是被“怀疑”会影响人工圈养的石龙子，并没有在野外石龙子身上“被证实”。

干扰 你可能会被原文的“infection with mites”迷惑，但要注意原文里的“怀疑”和“圈养”跟题目的“证实”和“野外”完全是反着来的。

句子 Although no direct health implications have been detected the trend is a concern, as it may signal a subtle deterioration in the skinks’ living environment. Infection with mites is suspected of inhibiting reproduction among captive animals.

Q35

解析 原文作者直接坦白，我们对应该为它们重建什么样的栖息地“毫无头绪”（haven’t a clue）。

干扰 你可能觉得科学家肯定知道理想的栖息地是什么样，但不要加入个人常识，原文明确表示目前相关知识极度匮乏。

句子 Even if we had the answer to the eradication of predators, we haven’t a clue to the habitat we should be recreating for the skinks, or if where they persist is best for conservation.

Q36

解析 原文明确提到，面对新西兰动物数量下降，人们总是首先怀疑是“被捕食”（predation）引起的。

干扰 你可能受干扰选项影响想选极端温度，但原文提下雪只是为了解释它们为什么不冬眠，并不是导致它们在野外活不长的主因。

句子 Unfortunately, extinction may loom for these reptiles. With any decline in New Zealand fauna, predation is always suspected, so the efforts of the Department of Conservation (DOC) have focused on controlling specific pests.

Q37

解析 原文明确指出，寄生虫感染的上升可能预示着它们的生活环境出现了轻微的“恶化”。

干扰 你可能会试图自己去推理寄生虫和数量的关系，但只需对准原文的“deterioration”，这就是选项中“decline in quality”的完美同义替换。

句子 Parasite infections are also thought to be on the rise. Although no direct health implications have been detected the trend is a concern, as it may signal a subtle deterioration in the skinks’ living environment.

Q38

解析 原文清楚地写着，800年前奥塔哥被森林覆盖，但是“大规模的焚烧”（extensive burning）改变了地貌。

干扰 你可能会因为不认识单词或者看错而选了种树，但原文的意思是原有的森林被大火烧光了变成了草地。

句子 Eight hundred years ago, Otago was covered in forest. However, extensive burning produced wide open tussock country.

Q39

解析 原文总结说，因为对它们的生态环境“缺乏基础知识”，导致有效的保护计划很难制定。

干扰 你可能想选资金不足或公众冷漠等雅思常见套路，但这段长句通篇都在强调我们“不了解”它们，也就是科学知识不足。

句子 A lack of fundamental knowledge about their ecology--what they eat, how they interact with other species, and their precise microhabitat needs--makes effective conservation planning difficult.

Q40

解析 原文列举了目前的保护努力，包括人工繁殖、防捕食者围栏和持续研究，唯独没有提到把它们“搬迁到新岛屿”。

干扰 做这种“NOT（未提及）”题不要凭空猜，只要在原文里用排除法划掉提到的A（围栏）、B（繁殖）、D（研究），剩下的C就是正确答案。

句子 Current efforts involve a combination of captive breeding programs, predator-free fencing around key sites, and ongoing research.
